metadata.description: The surface snapshot of the product on one declared version (PROP-057 `##OBS-SURFACE-SNAPSHOTS`, `##OBS-VERSION-CONTRACT`). It is a STRUCTURAL description and never a fingerprint: the command tree with its flags, the keys the manifest and the lock file accept, the members of every published schema, the text of every specification fact marked `actionstage="doc"`, and the format registry. There are no hashes, no build dates and no state identifiers anywhere in it — the only identity it carries is the version number the owner declared, because that number is the only event by which this project computes a difference between versions. Written by `vibe doc surface --record <version>` into `maintenance/surface/<version>.json` of a documentation package, read by `vibe doc diff <old> <new>`, and rendered by nothing: the directory is the documentation developers' kitchen and the site does not serve it (`##OBS-NOTHING-LEAKS`). Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/doc_surface/`.

The version number the caller declared, verbatim. It is an INPUT and never a reading: the product cannot tell one amend of a version from another, and a snapshot that guessed its own number would be pretending to a history the project does not keep (`##OBS-VERSION-CONTRACT`).

Every command of the binary, in the order a walk of `--help` reaches them, each with the flags it accepts. This is the surface a reader types, so it is taken from the help the reader would read and never from the parser's source.

Every dotted key path `vibe.toml` accepts, sorted — `package`, `package.title`, `package.binary[].name`. The list is what the real parser answers when asked, so it states what the product accepts rather than what a struct is called.
The same for `vibe.lock`.
Every JTD schema the format registry names, with its members. A document a foreign parser reads is a contract, and its members are the part of the contract a page quotes.

The text of every specification fact marked `actionstage="doc"` with an audience — the promises the documentation answers to. The TEXT is here and not a hash of it: a diff that could only say «this changed» would send a writer to read the whole corpus again.
The format registry as it stood, record by record.
One command of the binary and the flags it accepts.
The command line a reader types as far as this node — `vibe doc build`.
The one-line description the parent's help gives it, empty at the root.
One option of one command, as its own help spells it.
The long form when there is one, else the short — `--format`, `-h`.
The placeholder the flag takes, empty when it is a switch — `FORMAT`, `PATH`.
One published document format and the members its schema states.
The format id in the registry — the address that survives the file moving.
One member of one form of one schema.
The definition the member belongs to, empty for the document's own root.
Whether the member sits in `properties` rather than `optionalProperties`. Moving a member between the two is a contract change and this is what makes it visible.
The member's form in one phrase — `string`, `uint32`, `elements of doc_page`, `enum user|author`.
One documentation obligation of the specifications.
`<observed path>#<anchor>` — the address a page cites it by.
One record of `formats/REGISTRY.toml`, verbatim.
